test_title: PYST 17: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - GA (Held On 29 Jul, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statement about federalism in India is true?

options.text: States have the right to secede from the Union
There is rigid division of powers

solution:
The correct answer is __**The Union has overriding authority**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 1** of the **Constitution of India** describes India as a **"Union of States"** rather than a "Federation of States." This terminology signifies that the Indian federation is not the result of an agreement among the states, and consequently, no state has the **right to secede** from the Union. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*
 
• The Indian **federal system** follows a **flexible division of powers** rather than a rigid one. While the **Seventh Schedule** provides three lists (Union, State, and Concurrent), the Union government holds **residuary powers** and can influence state legislation under specific conditions. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• The **Union has overriding authority** over the states, which is a defining feature of India's **quasi-federal** structure. Under **Article 249**, Parliament can legislate on subjects in the State List in the **national interest** if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution. Similarly, during a **National Emergency (Article 352)**, the federal structure transforms into a unitary one. *Hence, statement 3 is correct.*
 
• In India, states are not **sovereign entities**. The **Parliament of India** has the power under **Article 3** to increase or diminish the area of any state, alter its boundaries, or change its name, even without the state legislature's ultimate consent. *Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.*
 
• The **supremacy of the Union** is also evident in the **Concurrent List**, where in case of a conflict between a central law and a state law, the **central law prevails** as per **Article 254**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nature of Indian Federalism:** 
 
 
• Experts like **K.C. Wheare** have described the Indian Constitution as **"quasi-federal"** because it contains both federal and unitary features with a strong tilt towards the **Center**.
 
• Other scholars, such as **Morris Jones**, termed it **"bargaining federalism,"** while **Granville Austin** called it **"cooperative federalism"** because of the interdependence between the Union and the States.
 
 
 
• **The Seventh Schedule:** 
 
 
• The **Union List** contains **100 subjects** (originally 97) such as **defense, foreign affairs, and banking**, over which only the Parliament can legislate.
 
• The **State List** consists of **61 subjects** (originally 66) like **police, public health, and agriculture**.
 
• The **Concurrent List** includes **52 subjects** (originally 47) such as **education, forests, and marriage**, where both tiers can legislate.
 
 
 
• **Unitary Features:** Features like a **Single Constitution**, **Single Citizenship**, **Integrated Judiciary**, and the appointment of the **Governor** by the **President** strengthen the Union's position.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **S.R. Bommai vs Union of India (1994):** In this landmark judgment, the **Supreme Court** ruled that **federalism** is a part of the **"Basic Structure"** of the Constitution. However, it also acknowledged the **superior powers** of the Union in matters of national integrity and security.
 
• **Residuary Powers:** Under **Article 248**, the power to legislate on any matter not mentioned in any of the three lists (Residuary Powers) is vested solely in the **Union Parliament**. This is a departure from the **U.S. federal model** where residuary powers rest with the states.
 
• **Article 356 (President's Rule):** This provision allows the Union to take over the **executive and legislative powers** of a state if the constitutional machinery fails, further illustrating the **overriding authority** of the Union.
